Description: No shift. The climate and price factors are drawn around their configured means.
Rationale: The comparator every other scenario is read against. Not a forecast.

Description: The regional climate factor is shifted two standard deviations down, so the regional yield falls by roughly 2 x yield_vol with the usual noise around it.
Rationale: A bad but ordinary year. The size is a judgement; it is the kind of year a lender should expect once a decade or so.

Description: The regional climate factor is shifted four standard deviations down: yields fall by roughly 45 percent at a 15 percent CV.
Rationale: LIT-031 records leaf rust across more than half of Central America's coffee area in one event, El Salvador output down 60 percent, and 80 percent drops at some financed producer organisations. A biological shock of that scale is outside a lognormal yield year and has to be imposed.

Description: The international reference price starts the season 35 percent below its configured base; the forward contract pays the agreed price on contracted volume.
Rationale: LIT-035 measures a 2019/20 intra-year range of 93.60 to 124.49 US cents/lb on the ICO composite, about a quarter peak to trough. A 35 percent fall is a stress beyond that measured range, by judgement.

Description: The reference price starts 40 percent above base, so spot runs far above the forward price and members have an incentive to side-sell committed crop.
Rationale: Tests the delivery-risk channel: a price rise is good for members and bad for a collective that has sold forward. The size is a judgement.

Description: A two-sigma climate shift and a 25 percent price fall together.
Rationale: The combination a lender fears: lower volume at lower prices, with the forward contract protecting only the contracted share. A coherence test, not a probability-weighted view.
